messages.author: ef49ed6122073bff
messages.subject: suspicious additional QTL
parts:
Hi Karl,

I recently encountered something strange. I have two families that were both derived from the same NIL. When I made linkage maps and ran QTL mapping for each family, I got a corroborating QTL in the two families in the MQM. This QTL is also indicated by one QTL scan in both families. I then integrated the maps of the two families and ran QTL mapping using the combined data from both families. I used family as a covariate. In the combined family mapping, the original QTL is still there, but I'm also getting a second QTL within 10 cM from the original QTL. This second QTL had even higher LOD score than the original QTL (while the LOD for the original QTL decreased substantially) and it took >50% of the phenotypic effect away. On the surface, it seems like a case where a larger sample size allowed us to split a QTL. But several signs suggest that the new QTL is suspicious. 

First, to explore the source of the second QTL, I ran QTL mapping on the integrated map in each family separately. In family 1, I'm stilling getting just the original QTL. The map of family 1 include markers associated with both the original and the new QTL. In family 2, I got the new QTL on the integrated map. But the linkage map of this family does not include markers associated with the new QTL (they were filtered out by segregation distortion). In other words, in family 2, using genotypes at additional markers on the integrated map that were not segregating according to the expected ratio, I'm getting an additional (and even more significant) QTL, which is counterintuitive as the genotype segregation pattern and the phenotype variation do not match well in this part of the map for family 2.

Of course just due to random chance, the phenotypic distribution is somewhat biased towards the right end. It is therefore likely that markers that do not fit the expected segregation ratio may actually fit better. However, I compared the genotype distribution at markers under the original and the new QTL, and the distribution at the original marker fits better with the phenotypic distribution.

Second, family 1 map contains the region associated with the new QTL but there is no evidence of a QTL in that region.

The two QTL has the same sign so they are not artificial QTL in repulsion. I am suspicious about the new QTL. I'm wondering if you have any suggestions on what else I should check to tell whether the new QTL is an artifact or not.

Many thanks and sorry for the long, complicated post.

Mingzi

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: suspicious additional QTL
parts:
I don't have any suggestions to offer, other than to go back to those markers in the first family, and consider the results with them included. You don't say enough about cross, sample size, size of QTL effects, or strength of evidence for these QTL to give much of a feel of the nature of things.

karl
